about: Global automaker formed in 2021 by the merger of Fiat Chrysler and PSA Group, owning brands such as Jeep, Ram, Dodge, Chrysler, Fiat, Peugeot, Citroen, Opel, Vauxhall, Alfa Romeo, Maserati and DS. Sells cars and light commercial vehicles to consumers and fleets in more than 130 markets, with roughly 250,000 employees and revenue above 150 billion euros. Legally based in Amsterdam, with major operations in Turin, Paris and Auburn Hills. Listed in Milan, Paris and New York (STLA). Household brands worldwide, very high consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Stellantis
wiki.text: Stellantis N.V. is a multinational automotive manufacturing corporation formed in 2021 through the merger of the French PSA Group and Italian-American Fiat Chrysler Automobiles (FCA), which was itself created by the merger of Italy's Fiat S.p.A. and the US-based Chrysler, completed in stages between 2009 and 2014. Stellantis is headquartered in Hoofddorp, Netherlands, while the CEO now operates from Auburn Hills, Michigan, United States.

about: Chinese new energy vehicle maker based in Hangzhou, selling compact electric cars such as the T03, C10 and B10 and range-extender models. Stellantis took a stake of about 21 percent in 2023 and formed Leapmotor International, a joint venture that sells the cars outside China from Hoofddorp, the Netherlands, through Stellantis dealers in Europe and other markets. Founded 2015 and listed in Hong Kong (9863). Budget-friendly electric brand with growing consumer visibility in Europe thanks to Stellantis distribution.
cb_desc: Leapmotor is a Hangzhou- based Chinese new energy car...

wiki.title: Leapmotor
wiki.text: Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology Co., Ltd., trading as Leapmotor, is a Chinese automobile manufacturer headquartered in Hangzhou, China, specializing in developing electric vehicles. The company was founded in 2015, and sold its first vehicles in 2019. In 2023, Stellantis acquired a 20 percent stake of Leapmotor, and started to sell Leapmotor vehicles in parts of Europe in 2024.

about: Chinese premium electric vehicle maker selling the NIO, ONVO and firefly brands, known for battery-swapping stations and a strong owner community. Customers are consumers, served via NIO House showrooms and direct sales in China and some European markets such as Germany and Norway. Headquartered in Shanghai; founded 2014 by William Li. Listed in New York (NIO), Hong Kong and Singapore. Delivers several hundred thousand vehicles a year and has long been loss-making. Recognised premium Chinese brand, a former Formula E team owner (now Jaguar's partner).

Chinese conglomerate and the world's largest maker of new energy vehicles, selling battery-electric and plug-in hybrid cars under BYD, Denza, Fangchengbao and Yangwang, plus buses, trucks, batteries, electronics components and solar products. Sells to consumers, fleets and transit agencies, with annual vehicle sales above 4 million and revenue well over 100 billion dollars. Headquartered in Shenzhen; founded 1995 by Wang Chuanfu. Listed in Hong Kong (1211) and Shenzhen, with Berkshire Hathaway historically a shareholder. Fast-growing global consumer brand, also a sports sponsor (UEFA Euro 2024).

wiki.title: BYD Company
wiki.text: BYD Company Limited or BYD is a Chinese multinational manufacturing conglomerate headquartered in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China. It is a vertically integrated company with several major subsidiaries, including BYD Auto which produces automobiles, BYD Electronics which produces electronic parts and assembly, and FinDreams, a brand name of multiple companies that produce automotive components and electric vehicle batteries.

about: Power technology manufacturer designing diesel, natural gas, electric and hydrogen engines, powertrains, generators, filtration, emissions and fuel systems. Customers are truck, bus, construction, mining and rail makers and power-generation users in about 190 countries, with revenue around 34 billion dollars and 70,000 employees. Headquartered in Columbus, Indiana; founded 1919. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (CMI). B2B brand with strong recognition among truckers and industrial buyers, and a history of motorsport involvement, including Indianapolis 500 sponsorship.

wiki.title: Cummins
wiki.what: American engines and related technology company
wiki.text: Cummins Inc. is an American multinational corporation that designs, manufactures, and distributes diesel engines, electric vehicle components, and power generation products. Cummins also services engines and related equipment, including fuel systems, air handling systems controls, filtration, emission control, electrical power generation systems, and engine control units.

about: Global automotive technology supplier created in 2022 when Faurecia acquired Hella, offering seating, interiors, clean mobility, lighting, electronics, lifecycle solutions and cockpit systems to carmakers. B2B, with annual sales of about 27 billion euros and roughly 150,000 employees across 40 countries. Headquartered in Nanterre, near Paris. Listed on Euronext Paris (FRVIA), with Stellantis a significant shareholder. Largely invisible to consumers but strong among car manufacturers; Hella and Faurecia brands carried prior motorsport and Le Mans ties.

wiki.title: Forvia
wiki.text: Forvia SE, formerly Faurecia SE, is a French global automotive supplier headquartered in Nanterre, in the western suburbs of Paris. In 2022 it was the 7th largest international automotive parts manufacturer in the world and #1 for vehicle interiors and emission control technology. One in two automobiles is equipped by Forvia. It designs and manufactures seats, exhaust systems, interior systems and decorative aspects of a vehicle.

about: Japanese automaker selling Nissan, Infiniti and Datsun vehicles, including the Leaf electric car, Ariya, Qashqai and the GT-R, with Renault and Mitsubishi in a long-standing alliance. Sells cars to consumers and fleets worldwide, producing several million vehicles a year and employing over 100,000 people. Headquartered in Yokohama; founded 1933. Listed in Tokyo (7201). Has been restructuring after sharp losses in 2024 and 2025. Household global brand, active in motorsport as a Formula E manufacturer, Super GT and a long-time FIFA and sports sponsor.

wiki.title: Nissan
wiki.text: Nissan Motor Co., Ltd., known simply as Nissan, trading as the Nissan Motor Corporation, and stylized as NISSAN, is a Japanese multinational automobile manufacturer headquartered in Yokohama, Kanagawa, Japan. The company sells its vehicles under the Nissan and Infiniti brands, and formerly the Datsun brand, with in-house performance tuning products under the Nismo and Autech brands. The company can be traced back to the beginning of the 20th century with the Nissan zaibatsu, or Nissan Group.

about: French automotive supplier producing driver-assistance sensors (lidar, radar, cameras), lighting, thermal systems, powertrain electrification and interior controls. Customers are global carmakers, with about 20 billion euros of revenue and some 100,000 employees across 29 countries; also an aftermarket parts distributor. Headquartered in Paris; founded 1923. Listed on Euronext Paris (FR). Strong industrial brand in the car industry, with limited consumer awareness although it has links to motorsport such as Le Mans and the World Endurance Championship.

wiki.title: Valeo
wiki.text: Valeo is a French global automotive supplier headquartered in France, listed on the Paris Stock Exchange. It supplies a wide range of products to automakers and the aftermarket. The Group employs 113,600 people in 29 countries worldwide. It has 186 production plants, 66 R&D centers and 15 distribution platforms. In 2018, Valeo's sales rose 4% to €19.1 billion. It frequently ranks as France's leading patent filer.

about: XPENG is a Chinese electric vehicle maker selling smart cars such as the G6, G9, P7+ and Mona models, plus developing flying cars through its Aeroht unit and humanoid robots. Sells to consumers in China and export markets in Europe and Asia, and relies on its in-house XNGP driver-assistance software; sells hundreds of thousands of vehicles yearly. Headquartered in Guangzhou; founded 2014. Listed in New York (XPEV) and Hong Kong (9868), with Volkswagen and Alibaba as investors. Tech-forward Chinese consumer brand expanding in Europe.

wiki.title: XPeng
wiki.text: Guangzhou Xiaopeng Motors Technology Co., Ltd., trading as XPeng Motors, commonly known as XPeng, is a Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer. The company is headquartered in Guangzhou, Guangdong, with offices in Mountain View, California, United States and Munich, Germany. XPeng stock is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The company describes itself as a global AI mobility technology company and develops in-house technologies including full-stack advanced driver-assistance systems, an in-car intelligent operating system, powertrain systems and vehicle electronic/electrical architecture.

about: Electric performance car brand spun out of Volvo Cars, selling the Polestar 2, 3, 4 and 5 to consumers online and through retail spaces in over 25 markets. Headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden, with plants in China and South Carolina and a design team in the UK. Controlled by Geely Holding and Volvo Cars, and listed on Nasdaq (PSNY) via a 2022 SPAC merger. It is loss-making and reliant on parent support. Premium design-led brand with growing awareness and prior motorsport and Formula-style marketing.

wiki.title: Polestar
wiki.text: Polestar Automotive Holding UK PLC, or simply Polestar, is a Swedish automotive manufacturer that produces electric cars. Principally owned by Li Shufu's PSD Investment, Geely Holding and Volvo Cars, the company is headquartered in Torslanda, outside Gothenburg, Sweden. With an "asset-light" approach in development and manufacturing, Polestar does not have its own manufacturing facility; instead it produces cars in facilities controlled by Volvo or Geely in several countries, including China, the United States, and South Korea.

about: Connectivity and sensor technology maker supplying connectors, sensors and harnesses to car makers, industrial automation, aerospace, medical, energy and data-center customers. B2B, with revenue around 16 billion dollars and roughly 90,000 employees in about 140 countries. Tax domicile in Switzerland and operational base in Galway, Ireland and Schaffhausen; US operations in Pennsylvania; spun out of Tyco in 2007. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (TEL). Component brand with little public awareness, though its sensors are in many vehicles.

wiki.title: TE Connectivity
wiki.text: TE Connectivity plc is an Irish-incorporated multinational company that designs and manufactures electrical connectors, sensors and other electronic components. Its products are used in the automotive, aerospace, defence, medical and energy industries, as well as industrial automation and data centers.

about: Diversified power management company making electrical products (switchgear, UPS, circuit breakers), hydraulics, aerospace fuel systems and vehicle components, plus data center power systems. Customers are utilities, data centers, industrial companies, aircraft makers and truck and car manufacturers, with revenue around 25 billion dollars and about 90,000 employees in over 160 countries. Headquartered in Dublin, Ireland; operational roots in Cleveland, Ohio, founded 1911. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ETN). B2B brand with modest consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Eaton Corporation
wiki.text: Eaton Corporation plc is an American-Irish multinational power management company, with global headquarters at the Eaton House in Dublin and a primary administrative center in Beachwood, Ohio. Eaton has more than 85,000 employees and sells products to customers in more than 175 countries.

about: Global automotive technology supplier producing vehicle architecture, active safety and ADAS software, connectors, wiring and displays for car makers; it has been separating its electrical distribution systems business. Customers are global automakers, with revenue around 20 billion dollars and over 100,000 employees. Legally domiciled in Schaffhausen, Switzerland; origins in Delphi Automotive with major operations in Troy, Michigan and Dublin. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (APTV). B2B brand with limited public awareness, though Aptiv has sponsored motorsport, notably as a Jaguar TCS Racing partner in Formula E.
cb_desc: Aptivis a global technology company that develops safer...

wiki.title: Aptiv
wiki.text: Aptiv PLC is a supplier of automotive technology and components. It is organized in Jersey and is a resident of Schaffhausen, Switzerland, for tax purposes. The company operates 139 major manufacturing facilities and 11 major technical centers and has a presence in 50 countries.

about: Largest automotive seating supplier in the world, designing and manufacturing seat structures, foam, trim and complete seats for major carmakers including Ford, Toyota, Volkswagen and Stellantis. Revenue is around 14 to 15 billion dollars from plants across more than 30 countries, with some 70,000 employees. Headquartered in Plymouth, Michigan, with Irish tax domicile; spun off from Johnson Controls in 2016. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ADNT). B2B brand with very limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Adient
wiki.text: Adient plc is an American, Irish-domiciled company that operates as the largest manufacturer of automotive seating for customers worldwide and is based in Plymouth, Michigan, United States.

about: Europe's largest wholesale and online used car trading platform, with the Autohero brand for retail sales and the wirkaufendeinauto.de service for consumer vehicle purchases. Buys cars from private sellers and dealers and sells to dealers across about 30 countries, selling hundreds of thousands of vehicles annually with revenue near 6 billion euros. Headquartered in Berlin; founded 2012. Listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (AG1) since 2021, with SoftBank a major backer. Autohero is a growing consumer brand; AUTO1 itself is largely B2B.

Avatr Technology is a Chinese premium electric vehicle brand owned by Changan Automobile with CATL and Huawei as technology and investment partners. Sells the Avatr 11, 12 and 07 models to consumers in China and has begun export. Based in Chongqing; launched 2018 as a Changan Automobile project. Has raised funding at multi-billion dollar valuations and filed for a Hong Kong listing. Rising smart EV brand with growing awareness in China and early international presence.
cb_desc: Avatr operates as an electric vehicle brand that focuses on...

wiki.title: Avatr Technology
wiki.text: Avatr Technology Co., Ltd. is a Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer headquartered in Chongqing.

about: Maker of recreational vehicles under the Sea-Doo, Ski-Doo, Can-Am off-road and on-road vehicles, Lynx snowmobile and Evinrude outboard brands. Sells to consumers through dealers worldwide with revenue around 8 billion Canadian dollars. Headquartered in Valcourt, Quebec; spun out of Bombardier in 2003 and now owned by the Beaudoin family and Bain Capital along with public shareholders. Listed on the Toronto and Nasdaq exchanges (DOO / BRP). Strong consumer brands and a regular sponsor of motorsport and action sports.

wiki.title: BRP Inc.
wiki.text: BRP Inc. is a Canadian manufacturer of snowmobiles, all-terrain vehicles, side by sides, motorcycles, and personal watercraft. It was founded in 2003, when the Recreational Products Division of Bombardier Inc. was spun off and sold to a group of investors consisting of Bain Capital, the Bombardier-Beaudoin family and the Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec. Bombardier Inc., was founded in 1942 as L'Auto-Neige Bombardier Limitée by Joseph-Armand Bombardier at Valcourt in the Eastern Townships, Quebec.

about: Geely Holding Group is a privately owned Chinese automotive group founded by Li Shufu in 1986, owning Volvo Cars, Polestar, Lotus, Zeekr, Lynk & Co, Geely Auto, LEVC and Proton stakes, and the Zeekr and Radar EV brands. Sells passenger cars worldwide, with groupwide sales above 3 million vehicles a year. Headquartered in Hangzhou, Zhejiang. Subsidiary Geely Automobile Holdings is listed in Hong Kong. Large global footprint but the Geely name itself is mainly recognised in Asia, Europe and emerging markets.

wiki.title: Geely
wiki.text: Zhejiang Geely Holding Group Co., Ltd. (ZGH), commonly known as Geely Holding, is a Chinese multinational automotive conglomerate headquartered in Hangzhou, China. The company was founded by, and is privately owned by Chinese entrepreneur Li Shufu.

about: British premium carmaker producing Jaguar, Land Rover, Range Rover and Defender vehicles, owned by India's Tata Motors since 2008. Sells luxury cars and SUVs globally, around 400,000 vehicles a year and revenue of about 29 billion pounds. Headquartered in Coventry, with plants in Solihull, Halewood and Slovakia and a rebrand toward an electric Jaguar from 2025. Wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Motors. Iconic consumer brands, with sponsorship experience in Formula E, sailing, cycling and the America's Cup.

wiki.title: Jaguar Land Rover
wiki.text: Jaguar Land Rover Automotive PLC (JLR) is a British multinational luxury automotive manufacturer and a wholly owned subsidiary of TATA.CARS. Headquartered in Whitley, Coventry, United Kingdom, the company specializes in designing, developing, manufacturing, and selling luxury automobiles under the brands Jaguar and Land Rover. It is one of the largest auto employers in the United Kingdom, with about 33,000 employees.

about: Canadian global automotive supplier and contract vehicle assembler producing body structures, seating, mirrors, powertrain systems and complete vehicles (Magna Steyr in Graz). Customers are global carmakers, with revenue around 40 billion dollars and about 170,000 employees. Headquartered in Aurora, Ontario; founded 1957 by Frank Stronach. Listed on the New York and Toronto stock exchanges (MGA). B2B, building cars for brands like BMW, Jaguar and Mercedes-Benz, with little consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Magna International
wiki.text: Magna International Inc. is a Canadian parts manufacturer for automakers. It is one of the largest companies in Canada and was recognized on the 2020 Forbes Global 2000. The company is the largest automobile parts manufacturer in North America by sales of original equipment parts; it has ranked consistently in the Fortune Global 500 list for 20 years in a row since 2001. It produces automotive systems, assemblies, modules, and components, which are supplied to General Motors, Ford and Stellantis, as well as BMW, Mercedes, Volkswagen, Toyota, Tesla, and Tata Motors, among others.

about: Geely Automobile Holdings is the main listed car-making arm of Geely Holding, producing Geely, Lynk & Co and Zeekr vehicles (Zeekr merged back in 2025), selling more than 2 million cars a year, plus exports. Customers are consumers in China and overseas. Headquartered in Hong Kong (Wan Chai) with operations in Hangzhou. Listed in Hong Kong (0175), controlled by Li Shufu. Large Chinese automaker with growing exports and a footprint in Europe via Lynk & Co.

wiki.title: Geely Auto
wiki.text: Geely Automobile Holdings Limited, commonly known as Geely Auto, is a publicly traded automotive company predominantly owned by the Zhejiang Geely Holding (ZGH) group. It owns the eponymous Geely Auto brand and partly owns Lynk & Co, Proton Cars and Zeekr brands. The company is incorporated in the Cayman Islands and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

about: Goodyear Tire & Rubber is one of the world's largest tire makers, selling tires under Goodyear, Dunlop, Cooper and Kelly brands for cars, trucks, aircraft and racing, plus retail and auto service centres. Customers are consumers, fleets and carmakers through dealers and owned stores, with sales near 19 billion dollars. Headquartered in Akron, Ohio; founded 1898. Listed on Nasdaq (GT). Iconic consumer brand and a long-time NASCAR, IndyCar and Le Mans partner, with the Goodyear blimp.

Vietnamese electric vehicle manufacturer producing the VF 3, VF 5, VF 6, VF 7, VF 8 and VF 9 models, a subsidiary of the conglomerate Vingroup, founded by Pham Nhat Vuong in 2017. Builds in Hai Phong, Vietnam and is constructing a plant in North Carolina and India. Sells cars and e-scooters to consumers in Vietnam, North America, Europe and Asia. Listed on Nasdaq (VFS) since a 2023 SPAC merger, with continuing losses. Strong in Vietnam, still emerging abroad, and has pursued sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: VinFast
wiki.text: VinFast Auto Ltd. is a Vietnamese multinational automotive manufacturer established in 2017 in Hải Phòng, Vietnam, as a subsidiary of Vingroup, one of the largest private conglomerates in Vietnam, founded by billionaire Phạm Nhật Vượng. It is the first Vietnamese automaker to sell passenger cars internationally and to manufacture electric vehicles, including electric cars and electric scooters.

about: Swedish-American automotive safety supplier, the world's largest maker of airbags, seatbelts and steering wheels for car makers, with sales near 10.5 billion dollars and about 65,000 employees at plants in 25 countries. Customers are global car companies. Legal headquarters in Stockholm, Sweden, with operations managed from Auburn Hills, Michigan; formed in 1997 by the merger of Autoliv and Morton ASP. Listed in Stockholm (ALIV SDB) and the New York Stock Exchange (ALV). B2B, limited consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Autoliv
wiki.text: Autoliv AB is a Swedish automotive safety supplier founded in Vårgårda in 1953, and headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden, It is the world’s largest automotive safety system supplier, producing systems such as airbags, seatbelts, and steering wheels for automotive manufacturers.

about: Swedish premium carmaker producing Volvo vehicles, with models such as the XC90, XC60, EX30 and EX90, known for safety. Sells about 700,000 cars a year to consumers worldwide with revenue near 400 billion Swedish kronor. Headquartered in Gothenburg; founded 1927 (Volvo Cars separate from AB Volvo trucks since 1999). Controlled by China's Geely Holding and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (VOLCAR B). Strong consumer brand and a past Formula E and sports sponsor.

wiki.title: Volvo Cars
wiki.what: Swedish multinational manufacturer of luxury vehicles
wiki.text: Volvo Car AB, trading as Volvo Cars, is a Swedish multinational manufacturer of luxury vehicles. Volvo is headquartered in Torslanda, Gothenburg. The company manufactures SUVs, station wagons, and sedans. The company's main marketing revolves around safety and its Swedish heritage and design.

about: German technology supplier of transmissions, chassis, driver assistance, electric drive and commercial vehicle systems, with sales near 40 billion euros and about 160,000 employees in around 30 countries. Customers are global car, truck and rail makers. Headquartered in Friedrichshafen; founded 1915 as Zahnradfabrik. Owned by the Zeppelin Foundation (majority) and Dr Jurgen and Irmgard Ulderup Foundation, so unlisted. Restructuring in 2024 and 2025 with job cuts. B2B brand with limited consumer awareness, though it is a visible motorsport sponsor, including Formula 1 and Sauber links.

wiki.title: ZF Friedrichshafen
wiki.text: ZF Friedrichshafen AG, also known as ZF Group, originally Zahnradfabrik Friedrichshafen, and commonly abbreviated to ZF, is a German technology manufacturing company that supplies systems for passenger cars, commercial vehicles and industrial technology. It is headquartered in Friedrichshafen, in the south-west German state of Baden-Württemberg. Specializing in engineering, it is primarily known for its design, research and development, and manufacturing activities in the automotive industry and is one of the largest automotive suppliers in the world.

about: Constellium is a global aluminium products maker producing rolled and extruded aluminium for aerospace, automotive and packaging, such as sheet for beverage cans and car body parts. Customers are industrial manufacturers, with revenue near 7 billion euros and about 12,000 employees. Headquartered in Paris with executive teams in Baltimore and Zurich; formed in 2011 from Alcan's engineered products. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (CSTM) and Euronext Paris. B2B manufacturer with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Constellium
wiki.text: Constellium SE is a French-based manufacturer and recycler of aluminium rolled products, extruded products and structural components. Constellium primarily serves the aerospace, automotive, and packaging sectors.

about: Japanese carmaker producing Subaru vehicles such as the Impreza, Forester, Outback, Crosstrek, WRX and BRZ, known for symmetrical all-wheel drive and boxer engines, along with aerospace products. Sells about 900,000 cars a year to consumers, mostly in North America. Headquartered in Tokyo; formerly Fuji Heavy Industries, renamed 2017. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (7270), with Toyota a major shareholder. Strong consumer brand in the US with a history in rallying and a long-time sponsor of sports.

wiki.title: Subaru Corporation
wiki.text: Subaru Corporation , formerly Fuji Heavy Industries, Ltd. , is a Japanese multinational corporation and conglomerate primarily involved in both terrestrial and aerospace transportation manufacturing. It is best known for its line of Subaru automobiles. Founded in 1953, the company was named Fuji Heavy Industries until 2017. The company's aerospace division is a defense contractor to the Japanese government, manufacturing Boeing and Lockheed Martin helicopters and airplanes under license. This same division is a global development and manufacturing partner to both companies.

about: Zipline designs, manufactures and operates autonomous delivery drones, which carry blood, medicines, groceries and food from fixed sites to homes and clinics. Started with medical deliveries in Rwanda and Ghana and now serves customers in the US, including Walmart and health systems. Headquartered in South San Francisco, California; founded 2014. Privately held with funding of about 2 billion dollars and a valuation above 4 billion dollars. Growing consumer visibility through retail partnerships.

wiki.title: Zipline (drone delivery company)
wiki.what: Company that delivers medical supplies by drone
wiki.text: Zipline International Inc. is an American company that designs, manufactures, and operates delivery drones, with distribution centers in the United States, Rwanda, Ghana, Japan, Nigeria, Côte d'Ivoire, and Kenya. As of January 2026, Zipline's drones have completed more than two million commercial deliveries and flown over 120 million miles.

about: Bolt is a European mobility and delivery platform, offering ride-hailing, e-scooters and bikes, food and grocery delivery (Bolt Food and Bolt Market) and car sharing in about 50 countries, in Europe and Africa. Founded 2013 in Tallinn, Estonia by Markus Villig. Privately held, valued at about 7.4 billion euros in 2022, with backers including Fidelity and Sequoia. Strong consumer brand in Europe and Africa and a sponsor in football, motorsport and other sports.

wiki.title: Bolt (company)
wiki.text: Bolt is an Estonian multinational mobility company that offers ride-hailing, micromobility rental, food and grocery delivery, and carsharing services. The company is headquartered in Tallinn and operates in over 850 cities in more than 50 countries in Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America.

about: Knorr-Bremse is a German maker of braking systems and safety technologies for rail vehicles and commercial vehicles, with revenue near 8 billion euros and 30,000 employees. Customers are train builders, truck makers and operators. Headquartered in Munich; founded 1905. Listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (KBX), with the Thiele family as controlling shareholder. B2B industrial brand with no consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Knorr-Bremse
wiki.text: Knorr-Bremse AG is a German manufacturer of braking systems for rail and commercial vehicles that has operated since 1905. Other products in the company's portfolio include intelligent door systems, control components, air conditioning systems for rail vehicles, torsional vibration dampers, and transmission control systems for commercial vehicles.

about: BorgWarner is an automotive supplier of powertrain and propulsion technologies, including turbochargers, transmissions components, electric drive modules, battery systems and charging. Customers are global carmakers and commercial vehicle makers, with revenue near 14 billion dollars. Headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan; founded 1928. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (BWA). B2B brand with little consumer awareness, though known in motorsport as the maker behind the Borg-Warner Trophy awarded to the Indianapolis 500 winner.

wiki.title: BorgWarner
wiki.text: BorgWarner Inc. is an American automotive and e-mobility supplier headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan. As of 2023, the company maintains production facilities and sites at 92 locations in 24 countries, and generates revenues of US$14.2 billion, while employing around 39,900 people. The company is one of the 25 largest automotive suppliers in the world. Since February 2025, Joseph F. Fadool has been CEO of BorgWarner Inc.

about: Michelin is a French tire maker producing Michelin, BFGoodrich, Kleber and Uniroyal tires (US licence), plus the Michelin Guide, maps and mobility experiences. Sells to carmakers, fleets and consumers through dealers, with revenue near 27 billion euros and about 125,000 employees. Headquartered in Clermont-Ferrand; founded 1889. Listed on Euronext Paris (ML). Famous consumer brand with a long history in motorsport as official tire supplier in MotoGP, WEC, Formula E and the Le Mans 24 Hours.

wiki.title: Michelin
wiki.text: Compagnie Générale des Établissements Michelin SCA, commonly referred to as Michelin, is a French multinational tyre manufacturer based in Clermont-Ferrand in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes région of France.

about: Bridgestone is the world's largest tire and rubber maker by revenue, producing Bridgestone, Firestone and Dayton tires, retail and auto service (Tires Plus, Hibdon), and industrial rubber. Customers are carmakers, fleets and consumers, with revenue near 4.3 trillion yen. Headquartered in Tokyo, with Bridgestone Americas based in Nashville, Tennessee. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (5108). Strong global brand and a long-standing sponsor of the Olympics, NFL, and Formula 1 history.

wiki.title: Bridgestone
wiki.text: Bridgestone Corporation is a Japanese multinational tire and rubber manufacturing company based in Kyōbashi, Tokyo. Founded in 1931 by Shōjirō Ishibashi in Kurume, it primarily manufactures tires, as well as golf equipment. In addition to automotive tires, the company produces tires for bicycles, motorcycles, and airplanes. The name Bridgestone comes from a calque translation and transposition of the founder's surname, meaning 'stone bridge' in Japanese.

about: KLA Corporation makes process control and yield management equipment for semiconductor manufacturing, including wafer inspection, metrology and process analysis tools sold to chipmakers such as TSMC, Samsung and Intel. Revenue near 12 billion dollars. Headquartered in Milpitas, California; formed by 1997 merger of KLA Instruments and Tencor. Listed on Nasdaq (KLAC). B2B equipment supplier with no consumer awareness; the input's automotive and distributor labels are inaccurate.

Gestamp is a Spanish automotive supplier specialising in metal components and structural parts such as body-in-white, chassis and press-hardened steel parts for carmakers, with revenue near 12 billion euros and plants in around 25 countries. Headquartered in Madrid (Abrera/Bizkaia origins); founded 1997 by the Riberas family, who remain the controlling shareholders. Listed on the Spanish stock exchanges (GEST). B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Gestamp
wiki.text: Gestamp Automoción, S.A. simply known as Gestamp is a Spanish multinational automotive engineering company. It is one of leading firms in the European automotive industry.

about: Zeekr is the premium electric vehicle brand of Geely Holding, based in Hangzhou, making models such as the Zeekr 001, 007, 009 MPV and X. It sells in China, Europe and other markets and listed on the NYSE (ZK) in 2024, then was taken private by Geely Automobile in a 2025 merger. Vehicle deliveries exceeded 200,000 a year. Strong Chinese premium EV brand, building awareness in Europe, with sponsorship activity in sport and F1-adjacent events.

wiki.title: Zeekr
wiki.text: Zeekr Intelligent Technology Holding Limited, trading as Zeekr Group, is a Chinese automobile company. It is wholly owned by Geely Automobile Holdings.

about: Hyundai Mobis is a Seoul-based South Korean auto parts maker, the largest supplier to Hyundai Motor Group, producing modules (chassis, cockpit, front-end), electrification parts, ADAS sensors, lamps and aftermarket parts, with global sales near KRW 60 trillion. It also runs a Mobis parts aftersales business. Listed on the Korea Exchange (012330), with Hyundai-affiliated groups as major shareholders. Mostly B2B, known to the auto industry, with limited consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Hyundai Mobis
wiki.text: Hyundai Mobis Company Limited (Korean: 현대모비스), commonly known as Hyundai Mobis, is a public South Korean car parts company which is a member of Hyundai Motor Group. Founded in 1977, the company currently forms the "parts and service" arm for the South Korean automakers Hyundai Motor Company, Genesis Motors and Kia Motors. As of 2025, it was the "world's No. 6 automotive supplier".

about: Horse Powertrain is a London-registered powertrain company formed in 2022 as a joint venture between Renault Group and Geely, with Aramco joining as a 10 percent investor in 2024. It builds combustion engines, hybrid systems and transmissions, with plants and R&D in Europe, Brazil, China and Turkey, and about 19,000 employees. Customers include Renault, Dacia, Geely brands and other carmakers. B2B component maker, with the Horse name known in the car industry only.

wiki.title: Horse Powertrain
wiki.text: Horse Powertrain Limited is a joint venture holding aimed at producing powertrains, including internal combustion engines (ICE) and hybrid systems. The venture holding was established in May 2024 and is equally owned by Renault and Geely. It is headquartered in London, United Kingdom.

about: Rimac Group is a Croatian electric hypercar and technology company based near Zagreb, formed from Rimac Automobili (maker of the Nevera) and Bugatti Rimac, which owns Bugatti, and Rimac Technology, a supplier of battery systems and drivetrains for carmakers such as Porsche, Aston Martin and Koenigsegg. Founded by Mate Rimac in 2009, its investors include Porsche (about 45 percent) and Hyundai/Kia. Private. Very high profile among car enthusiasts, with its hypercar sales limited to a few hundred units.

Garmin is a GPS technology company, legally Swiss and operating from Olathe, Kansas, making GPS wearables and smartwatches (Forerunner, fenix, Venu), cycling computers, marine electronics, aviation avionics, automotive navigation and in-car systems. It sells to consumers and OEM customers worldwide, with revenue near $7bn and about 20,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (GRMN). Strong consumer brand among athletes, pilots and boaters, and a sports sponsor including sailing, cycling and motorsport.

wiki.title: Garmin
wiki.text: Garmin Ltd. is an American multinational technology company based in Olathe, Kansas. The company designs, develops, manufactures, markets, and distributes GPS-enabled products and other navigation, communication, sensor-based, and information products to the automotive, aviation, marine, outdoors, and sport markets.

about: Chery Holding is a Wuhu, China-based state-linked automaker, one of China's largest carmakers and top vehicle exporters, owning the Chery, Exeed, Jetour, iCar and Omoda brands and a joint venture with JLR (Freelander in China). It sells passenger cars and SUVs, including EVs, in over 100 countries. Its subsidiary Chery Automobile listed in Hong Kong in 2025 (9973). Consumer car brand with growing recognition in Europe, Latin America and emerging markets, and a football and sports sponsor.

wiki.title: Chery
wiki.text: Chery Automobile Co. Ltd., trading as Chery, is a Chinese automobile manufacturer. Founded in 1997, it is currently the fifth largest automobile manufacturer group in China, with 2,806,393 vehicles sold in 2025. The company is headquartered in Wuhu, Anhui.

about: Linamar is a Guelph, Ontario-based Canadian precision manufacturer of vehicle powertrain components, drivetrain systems and structural parts, plus Skyjack access platforms and agricultural equipment (MacDon). Customers are global automakers such as GM, Ford and Stellantis. Founded in 1966 by Frank Hasenfratz, it has about 32,000 employees in 17 countries and revenue near C$10 billion. Listed on the TSX (LNR). B2B supplier with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Linamar
wiki.text: Linamar Corporation is a manufacturing company serving the mobility, access, agriculture, and MedTech industries. The company has three operating segments: Industrial, Mobility, and eLIN.

about: Sokon is a Chinese automotive manufacturer (Chongqing Sokon Industry Group, brand Seres, associated with the Seres-Huawei Aito partnership) that develops and manufactures automobiles, new energy vehicles and engines. Seres Group is listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong. The input lists funding of about 7.1 billion yuan. Consumer-facing through Aito vehicles in China, but little brand awareness abroad.
cb_desc: Sokon engages in the research and development...

wiki.title: Seres Group
wiki.text: Seres Group (赛力斯集团股份有限公司) is a Chinese automotive manufacturer founded in September 1986 with headquarters in Chongqing, China. Born as a manufacturer of components for household appliances and shock absorbers, it currently produces electric cars, ICEs cars, motorcycles and commercial vehicles as well as shock absorbers and internal combustion engines. In 2022, the company renamed to Seres Group from Sokon Group. It operates through its subsidiaries Seres, Seres Hubei, XGJAO Motorcycle and Yu'an Shock Absorber Company.

about: ABB is a Zurich-based Swiss-Swedish multinational technology group in electrification, automation, motion and robotics, serving utilities, industry, transport and buildings in about 100 countries. Revenue is roughly $33 billion, with about 110,000 employees. It also runs the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship title sponsorship and EV charging (Terra chargers). Listed on SIX Swiss Exchange and Nasdaq Stockholm (ABBN). B2B, high business awareness and a notable sports sponsor.

wiki.title: ABB
wiki.text: ABB Group is a Swedish-Swiss technology company, that operates in the fields of electrification and automation. The company was formed in 1988 from the merger of two electrical engineering companies, ASEA of Sweden and Brown, Boveri & Cie (BBC) of Switzerland.

about: BMW Group is a Munich-based luxury automaker founded in 1916, producing BMW, MINI and Rolls-Royce cars and BMW Motorrad motorcycles. It sells around 2.5 million vehicles a year across 140 countries with revenue near 140 billion euros and about 150,000 employees. Listed on the Frankfurt exchange (BMW) and controlled by the Quandt family. Customers are consumers and fleets. Global premium brand with a long history in motorsport and in F1 sponsorship and partnerships.

wiki.title: BMW
wiki.text: Bayerische Motoren Werke AG, trading as BMW Group, is a German multinational conglomerate manufacturer of luxury vehicles and motorcycles headquartered in Munich, Germany. The moniker "BMW" first came into use when the German firm Rapp Motorenwerke changed its name to Bayerische Motoren Werke GmbH in 1917. Thereafter, in 1922, the name and assets of BMW GmbH were transferred to the aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke AG, thereby giving rise to the company known today as BMW AG.

about: Guangzhou Automobile Group (GAC Group) is a Guangzhou, China state-owned automaker, listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong (601238, 2238), making vehicles under GAC Trumpchi, GAC Aion (EV) and Hyptec, and in joint ventures with Toyota, Honda and Mitsubishi. It also has financial services and parts businesses. Sells hundreds of thousands to over 2 million vehicles a year. Strong consumer brand in China and a growing export business.

wiki.title: GAC Group
wiki.text: Guangzhou Automobile Group Co., Ltd. is a Chinese state-owned automobile manufacturer headquartered in Guangzhou, Guangdong. As of 2021, it was the fifth largest automobile manufacturer in China, with 2.144 million sales in 2021.

about: Sonic Automotive is a Charlotte, North Carolina-based automotive retailer, a Fortune 500 company listed on NYSE (SAH), operating about 100 franchised dealerships and EchoPark pre-owned stores in the US, and was the first to adopt a no-haggle pricing model for used cars. Revenue is above $14 billion. Controlled by the Smith family. Customers are US car buyers. Strong local brand, with a motorsport legacy via Speedway Motorsports (spun out).

wiki.title: Sonic Automotive
wiki.text: Sonic Automotive is a Fortune 500 company based in Charlotte, North Carolina, and is the fifth largest automotive retailer in the United States as measured by total revenues. The company was founded by O Bruton Smith and completed its initial public offering on the NYSE in 1997.

about: Mitsubishi Motors is a Japanese automaker headquartered in Tokyo, producing the Outlander, Eclipse Cross, Pajero and Triton, with major sales in Southeast Asia, Australia, Europe and North America and revenue near 2.5 trillion yen. Nissan holds about 34 percent, and it is part of the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi Alliance. Founded 1970 from Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. Strong motorsport history, including Dakar Rally and WRC wins, and consumer brand awareness especially in Asia.

wiki.title: Mitsubishi Motors
wiki.text: Mitsubishi Motors Corporation is a Japanese multinational automobile manufacturer headquartered in Minato, Tokyo, Japan. In 2011, Mitsubishi Motors was the sixth-largest Japanese automaker and the 19th-largest worldwide by production. Mitsubishi Motors took over as the 16th largest automaker worldwide by production in 2012. Since October 2016 Mitsubishi has been included in the Renault–Nissan–Mitsubishi Alliance, with Nissan owning a one-third stake in Mitsubishi from that time until November 2024, when their stake was scaled down to one quarter.

about: Dana is a supplier of drivetrain and propulsion technology: axles, driveshafts, transmissions, e-motors, inverters and sealing and thermal-management products for light vehicles, commercial trucks, off-highway machinery and electric vehicles. Customers are vehicle manufacturers such as Ford, Stellantis and Cummins, with revenue of about $10 billion. Headquartered in Maumee, Ohio, with operations in about 30 countries. Listed on NYSE (DAN). In 2025 it agreed to sell its off-highway business to Allison Transmission. B2B supplier, little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Dana (company)
wiki.text: Dana, proizvodnja in prodaja pijač is a major Slovenian manufacturer of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages. It is located in the village of Mirna in southeastern Slovenia.

about: Piaggio Group is Europe's largest scooter and motorcycle maker, owning Piaggio, Vespa, Aprilia, Moto Guzzi and Gilera, plus the Ape three-wheel commercial vehicles. Customers are consumers and businesses in Europe, India, Vietnam and the US. Headquartered in Pontedera, Tuscany, it was founded in 1884, with about 5,000 employees and revenue of roughly 1.7 billion euros. Listed on Borsa Italiana (PIA), majority controlled by Immsi. Strong consumer brands, with Aprilia in MotoGP racing.

wiki.title: Piaggio
wiki.text: Piaggio Group is an Italian motor vehicle manufacturer, which produces a range of two-wheeled motor vehicles and compact commercial vehicles under five brands: Piaggio, Vespa, Aprilia, Moto Guzzi and Derbi. Its corporate headquarters are located in Pontedera, Italy. The company was founded by Rinaldo Piaggio in 1884, initially producing locomotives and railway carriages.

about: Apollo Tyres is an Indian tyre maker producing passenger car, SUV, truck, bus, farm and two-wheeler tyres under Apollo and Vredestein brands, with plants in India, the Netherlands and Hungary. Customers are consumers, fleets and vehicle manufacturers in more than 100 countries, with revenue over INR 25,000 crore. Founded in 1972 and headquartered in Gurugram. Listed on NSE and BSE (APOLLOTYRE). Known for sports sponsorship, including Indian cricket and a long-running Manchester United partnership, so well-known consumer brand.

wiki.title: Apollo Tyres
wiki.text: Apollo Tyres Limited is an Indian multinational tyre manufacturing company headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana. It was incorporated in 1972, and its first plant was commissioned in Perambra, Kerala. The company now has five manufacturing units in India, one in the Netherlands and one in Hungary. As of 2024, the company generates 87% of its revenues from India, 11% from Europe and 2% from other countries.

about: Tata Motors is India's largest automaker by revenue and part of the Tata Group, making passenger cars and SUVs (Nexon, Punch, Harrier, Safari), electric vehicles, and commercial trucks and buses, and owning Jaguar Land Rover. In October 2025 it was demerged into a passenger vehicle business (including JLR) and a commercial vehicle business. Listed on the NSE and BSE. Crunchbase shows Pune as the location. Very strong consumer brand in India and globally through JLR.

wiki.title: Tata Motors
wiki.text: Tata Motors Limited, also known as Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles, is an Indian multinational commercial vehicle manufacturer, headquartered in Mumbai and is a part of the Tata Group. The company produces trucks, vans, and buses.

about: TVS Motor Company is a major Indian two-wheeler and three-wheeler maker, producing the Apache, Jupiter, Raider, iQube electric scooter and Ntorq brands, and owning Norton Motorcycles and the Swiss E-Mobility Group. Headquartered in Chennai (Crunchbase lists the Hosur plant). Sells in over 80 countries with annual revenue of around INR 35,000 crore. Part of the TVS Group. Listed on the NSE and BSE. Strong consumer brand, active in motorsport with TVS Racing.

wiki.title: TVS Motor Company
wiki.text: TVS Motor Co., Ltd. is an Indian multinational motorcycle manufacturer headquartered in Chennai. It is the third-largest motorcycle company in India by revenue. The company has annual sales of three million units and an annual production capacity of over four million vehicles. TVS Motor Company is also the second largest two-wheeler exporter in India with exports to over 60 countries.

about: Japanese commercial vehicle and diesel engine maker based in Yokohama, founded 1937, producing Isuzu trucks, buses and the D-Max pickup, sold in about 100 countries with strong Southeast Asian presence. Revenue is about JPY 3 trillion. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (7202). Known to commercial customers worldwide; the D-Max is a familiar consumer pickup in several markets. Isuzu employs about 45,000 people, builds trucks and engines in Japan, Thailand and the US, and works closely with Toyota and Hino.

wiki.title: Isuzu
wiki.text: Isuzu Motors Ltd. is a Japanese multinational automobile manufacturer headquartered in Yokohama, Kanagawa Prefecture. Its principal activity is the production, marketing and sale of Isuzu commercial vehicles and diesel engines.

about: Voyah is the premium electric vehicle brand of Dongfeng Motor Group, a Chinese state-owned automaker, selling the Free, Dreamer, Passion and Chaser models in China and abroad. It is sold in markets including Norway, where the Crunchbase entry places its European headquarters in Oslo, with exports across Europe, the Middle East and Southeast Asia. Customers are consumers and fleets buying plug-in hybrid and electric vehicles. Dongfeng restructured its listing in Hong Kong and moved Voyah toward a 2025 Hong Kong listing via a reverse takeover. Moderate consumer awareness in China, still building in Europe.

wiki.title: Voyah
wiki.text: Voyah is the luxury subsidiary of Chinese state-owned automaker Dongfeng Motor Corporation. Voyah was founded in April 2019, specializing in designing and developing premium electric vehicles. Dongfeng Motor Corporation unveiled its brand logo at the Big House Contemporary Art Center in Wuhan on 17 July 2020.

about: Nokian Tyres is a Finnish tyre manufacturer, based in Nokia near Tampere, known for winter tyres and the invention of the winter tyre in 1934, selling passenger car, van, truck and agricultural tyres under the Nokian and Vianor retail brands. It has factories in Finland, the United States (Dayton, Tennessee) and Romania, and is listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (TYRES). Revenue is about 1.3 billion euros. Strong in the Nordics and North America with motorsport and rally associations.

wiki.title: Nokian Tyres
wiki.text: Nokian Tyres plc is a Finnish tyre manufacturer headquartered in Nokia, Finland, which produces tyres for cars, trucks, buses, and heavy-duty equipment. Known for its winter tyres, Nokian is the only tyre manufacturer in the world with its own permanent winter tyre testing facility. The company's Hakkapeliitta brand name is recognised in Finland as a trademark.

about: CEAT is an Indian tyre manufacturer, part of the RPG Group, headquartered in Mumbai, producing tyres for motorcycles, scooters, cars, SUVs, trucks, buses, tractors and off-highway vehicles. It sells in India through thousands of dealers and exports to over 100 countries, with plants in Nashik, Halol, Nagpur and Chennai. Listed on the NSE and BSE, with revenue around 130 billion rupees. Well-known consumer brand in India, strongly linked with cricket sponsorship.

wiki.title: CEAT Limited
wiki.text: CEAT Limited is an Indian multinational tyre manufacturing company owned by the RPG Group. It was established in 1924 in Turin, Italy, and acquired by RPG Group in 1982. CEAT produces over 48 million tyres a year and manufactures them for cars, two-wheelers, trucks, buses, light commercial vehicles, earth-movers, forklifts, tractors, trailers, and auto-rickshaws. The current capacity of CEAT tyres plants is over 800 tonnes per day. The company has manufacturing plants in Halol, Butibori, Bhandup, Nashik, Ambernath, and Chennai.

about: ABB E-Mobility is the electric vehicle charging division of Swiss technology group ABB, making DC fast chargers (Terra series), AC wallboxes and charging software for fleets, charge point operators and automakers, with manufacturing in Europe, the US and China. ABB itself is based in Zurich and listed on SIX Swiss Exchange and NYSE (ABB). The Crunchbase industry label is inaccurate. B2B charging hardware supplier; ABB is well known, and has a Formula E title sponsorship history.
cb_desc: ABB's E-Mobility division remotely diagnose, cure...

about: US iconic motorcycle maker founded 1903 in Milwaukee, listed on NYSE (HOG). Sells cruiser and touring motorcycles through dealers globally, owns LiveWire. Strong global consumer brand.

wiki.title: Harley-Davidson
wiki.text: Harley-Davidson, Inc. is an American motorcycle manufacturer and lifestyle brand headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Founded in 1903, it is one of two major American motorcycle manufacturers to survive the Great Depression along with its historical rival, Indian Motorcycle Company. The company has survived numerous ownership arrangements, subsidiary arrangements, periods of poor economic health and product quality, and intense global competition to become an iconic brand widely known for its loyal following. There are owner clubs and events worldwide, as well as a company-sponsored, brand-focused museum.

about: Swedish Volvo Group, maker of Volvo trucks, buses and construction equipment, Mack and Renault Trucks, based in Gothenburg. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Revenue about SEK 550 billion. Separate from Volvo Cars. Brands include Renault Trucks, Mack, UD Trucks, Prevost, Nova Bus and Volvo Penta marine engines. Volvo Cars was sold to Ford in 1999. Strong B2B brand, sponsor of sports.

wiki.title: Volvo
wiki.text: Aktiebolaget Volvo, doing business as Volvo Group is a Swedish multinational manufacturing corporation headquartered in Gothenburg. While its core activity is the production, distribution and sale of trucks, buses and construction equipment, Volvo also supplies marine and industrial drive systems and financial services. In 2016, it was the world's second-largest manufacturer of heavy-duty trucks through its subsidiary Volvo Trucks.

about: Chery Automobile is a Chinese carmaker based in Wuhu, Anhui, founded in 1997, producing petrol, hybrid and electric cars sold under Chery, Exeed, Jetour, Jaecoo, Omoda and iCar brands. It is one of China's biggest auto exporters, selling in dozens of countries including Russia, Latin America and Europe. It listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2025. Customers are consumers. Growing global consumer brand with strong awareness in emerging markets.
flags: last funding 2009: check it is still independent and operating

wiki.title: Chery
wiki.text: Chery Automobile Co. Ltd., trading as Chery, is a Chinese automobile manufacturer. Founded in 1997, it is currently the fifth largest automobile manufacturer group in China, with 2,806,393 vehicles sold in 2025. The company is headquartered in Wuhu, Anhui.

about: Mahindra & Mahindra is a Mumbai-based Indian conglomerate and one of the country's largest vehicle makers, producing SUVs such as the Thar, Scorpio and XUV700, tractors, commercial vehicles and electric vehicles, plus services in finance, hospitality and IT through group companies. Founded in 1945, it is listed on the NSE and BSE. Customers are Indian and international buyers. Very high consumer awareness in India, and active in sport and Formula E.

wiki.title: Mahindra & Mahindra
wiki.text: Mahindra & Mahindra Limited (M&M) is an Indian automobile manufacturing company, headquartered in Mumbai. It was established in 1945 as Mahindra & Mohammed and later renamed Mahindra & Mahindra. Part of the Mahindra Group, Mahindra Automotive is one of the largest SUV manufacturers by production in India and Mahindra Tractors is the largest manufacturer of tractors in the world by volume. The company also manufactures commercial vehicles through its Truck and Bus Division and SML Mahindra subsidiary.

about: Denso is a Japanese automotive components giant headquartered in Kariya, Aichi, with a major North American base in Southfield, Michigan. It makes thermal, powertrain, electrification, mobility electronics and safety systems for carmakers, with Toyota as the top customer and about 7 trillion yen in revenue and 160,000-plus employees. Listed in Tokyo (6902), with Toyota Group as the main shareholder. Denso is a well-known Formula 1-adjacent industrial brand with global motorsport involvement in Japan.

wiki.title: Denso
wiki.text: Denso Corporation is a global automotive components manufacturer headquartered in the city of Kariya, Aichi Prefecture, Japan.

about: Ninebot is a Chinese personal transportation and robotics maker, headquartered in Beijing (listed on the Shanghai STAR market as Ninebot Ltd.), which produces electric scooters, self-balancing devices and delivery robots. It acquired Segway in 2015 and sells Segway-Ninebot products worldwide, with Xiaomi as an early investor. Revenue is around 15 billion yuan. Recognised consumer brand in e-mobility.

wiki.title: Segway Inc.
wiki.what: Chinese-acquired American maker of self-balancing personal transporters
wiki.text: Segway Inc. is a Chinese-owned, formerly American manufacturer of two-wheeled personal transporters, chiefly through its Segway PT and Segway miniPro product lines. Founded by inventor Dean Kamen in 1999, the company's name is a homophone of the word "segue".

about: Honeywell Aerospace makes aircraft engines (auxiliary power units, turbofans), avionics, cockpit systems, braking, satellites and parts and services for commercial, defence and space customers. Revenue near 15 billion dollars. Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. A segment of Honeywell, which has planned to spin it off as a separate listed company in the second half of 2026. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Honeywell Aerospace
wiki.text: Honeywell Aerospace Inc. is an independent American manufacturer of aircraft engines, avionics, auxiliary power units (APUs), navigation equipment, life-support and environmental control systems, hydraulics, flight data recorders, and other aviation and space systems. Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, it operates as one of the world's largest standalone tier-1 aerospace and defense suppliers. The company generates approximately $15 billion in annual revenue from a balanced portfolio of commercial and military defense contracts.

about: Bombardier is a Canadian manufacturer of business jets, including the Challenger and Global families (Global 7500 and 8000), with servicing and defence modifications. Sells to wealthy individuals, corporates and governments, with revenue near 8 billion dollars. Headquartered in Montreal, Quebec; founded 1942. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (BBD.B). It sold its rail business to Alstom in 2021 and aerospace commercial units earlier. Premium aviation brand with narrow audience.

wiki.title: Bombardier Inc.
wiki.text: Bombardier Inc. is a Canadian manufacturer of business jets. Headquartered in Montreal, the company was founded in 1942 in Valcourt by Joseph-Armand Bombardier to market his snowmobiles, later to become one of the world's largest producers of aircraft and trains until divestiture in the 21st century.

about: Qnity Electronics is a Wilmington, Delaware company spun out from DuPont in November 2025, supplying materials and technology for semiconductor manufacturing and advanced electronics, including CMP pads and slurries, photoresists and interconnect materials. Customers are chipmakers like TSMC, Samsung and Intel and electronics manufacturers worldwide, with annual revenue near $4 billion. Listed on NYSE (Q). B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Qnity Electronics
wiki.what: American provider of materials for the semiconductor and electronics industries
wiki.text: Qnity Electronics, Inc. is a major provider of materials for the semiconductor manufacturing and electronics industries headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware. The company's Semiconductor Technologies segment produces products for chemical-mechanical polishing, photolithography, sealing applications, and OLED displays. Its Interconnect Solutions segment provides products for signal integrity, including semiconductor coatings, thermal and electromagnetic shielding, and laminate materials. Kapton is a brand of the company.

about: Rolls-Royce Holdings is a London-based engineering company making civil and defence aerospace engines (Trent, Pearl, Adour), nuclear submarine reactors, small modular reactors and Power Systems (mtu engines, power generation). Rolls-Royce Motor Cars, the luxury car maker, is owned separately by BMW. Revenue is around 18 billion pounds. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (RR.). Customers are airlines, airframers, and governments. Strong global brand, with aerospace sponsorship and heritage.

wiki.title: Rolls-Royce
wiki.what: List of articles associated with the British automobile and engine manufacturer
wiki.text: Rolls-Royce may refer to:Rolls-Royce Limited, a British manufacturer of cars and later aircraft engines, founded in 1906, now defunct Rolls-Royce Motors, owner of the former car division incorporated in 1973 and folded in 1998 Rolls-Royce Motor Cars, the current car manufacturing company incorporated in 1998, a subsidiary of BMW Group Rolls-Royce Holdings plc, an aerospace, power systems and defence company and Rolls-Royce's current principal operating company Rolls-Royce Controls and Data Services Rolls-Royce Deutschland Rolls-Royce Power Systems Rolls-Royce North America Rolls-Royce Submarines Rolls-Royce Turbomeca

about: Air China is a Beijing-based Chinese flag carrier, a state-owned airline of the Air China Group, operating domestic and international passenger and cargo flights from hubs at Beijing Capital and Chengdu, with about 700 aircraft, and a member of the Star Alliance. Listed in Hong Kong, Shanghai and London (753, 601111). Controlled by China National Aviation Holding. Very high brand awareness in China, and an Olympic and sports partner.

wiki.title: Air China
wiki.what: Flag carrier airline of the People's Republic of China
wiki.text: Air China, officially Air China Limited, is the flag carrier airline of the People's Republic of China. It is headquartered in Shunyi, Beijing. The airline offers both domestic and international flights to different destinations around China and the world.

about: Air France-KLM is a Paris-based airline group formed in 2004 by the merger of Air France and KLM, also owning Transavia and Martinair, with about 550 aircraft carrying around 100 million passengers a year. Listed on Euronext Paris and Amsterdam (AF), with the French state holding around 28 percent. Revenue is about 31 billion euros. Very high consumer brand awareness in Europe, and a sports and cultural sponsor.

wiki.title: Air France–KLM
wiki.text: Air France–KLM S.A., also known as Air France–KLM Group, is a French–Dutch multinational airline holding company with its headquarters in the Rue du Cirque, Paris, France. The group's three major brands are Air France, KLM and Transavia. Air France–KLM is the result of the merger in 2004 between Air France and KLM. Both Air France and KLM are members of the SkyTeam airline alliance. The group's main hubs are Paris–Charles de Gaulle Airport, Paris Orly Airport and Amsterdam Airport Schiphol. Air France–KLM airlines transported 83 million passengers in 2022.

about: AviLease is a Riyadh-based Saudi aircraft lessor owned by the Public Investment Fund, established in 2022, which buys and leases narrow- and wide-body aircraft to airlines and has placed large Airbus and Boeing orders. The input shows about $3.7 billion in funding. B2B aircraft leasing, with no consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: AvilLease, an aircraft lessor with a portfolio of the latest...

about: Azul is a Sao Paulo-based Brazilian airline, founded in 2008 by David Neeleman, serving more than 150 destinations, mostly domestic, from its Campinas hub, with loyalty program TudoAzul. It carries about 30 million passengers a year and is listed on B3 and NYSE (AZUL). It filed for Chapter 11 in 2025. Consumers are Brazilian travellers. Strong consumer brand in Brazil, with football sponsorship.

Dubai Aerospace Enterprise (DAE) is an aviation services company headquartered in Dubai, owned by the Investment Corporation of Dubai. It is one of the world's largest aircraft lessors (DAE Capital) with hundreds of aircraft, and also runs engineering and maintenance (DAE Engineering) and a regional MRO. Customers are airlines around the world; revenue comes from lease rentals and MRO services. Founded 2006. B2B aviation business with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Dubai Aerospace Enterprise
wiki.text: Dubai Aerospace Enterprise Ltd (DAE) is an aviation services corporation with two divisions: DAE Capital and DAE Engineering. Headquartered in Dubai, DAE serves over 200 airline customers in over 85 countries from its eight office locations in Dubai, Dublin, London, Amman, Singapore, Miami, Seattle, and San Francisco.

about: IndiGo (InterGlobe Aviation) is India's largest airline by market share, with over 60 percent of domestic traffic and a fleet of 400 plus Airbus A320 family and ATR aircraft, flying to dozens of international destinations. Headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana, it was founded in 2006 and is listed on the NSE and BSE. It operates a low-cost model with ancillary revenue, and carries around 100 million passengers a year. Strong mass-market consumer brand in India and a large advertiser.

wiki.title: IndiGo
wiki.text: IndiGo is an Indian low-cost airline headquartered in Gurgaon, Haryana. It is the largest airline in India by passengers carried, with a 64.2% domestic market share as of August 2025. It is one of the largest in the world in terms of passengers carried, with 31.9 million passengers carried in the fourth quarter of 2025. It is the sixth busiest airline in the world, as per data from RadarBox. As of November 2025, IndiGo operates over 2,700 daily flights to 137 destinations – 94 domestic and 43 international. It operates cargo services under its subsidiary, IndiGo CarGo. Its primary hub is located at Indira Gandhi International Airport in Delhi

about: Samvardhana Motherson International (SAMIL) is the flagship company of India's Motherson Group, headquartered in Noida and listed on the NSE and BSE. It makes wiring harnesses, rear-view mirrors, plastic modules, bumpers and aerospace and medical components for car makers such as Volkswagen, Mercedes, BMW and Toyota, with 400 or so plants in about 40 countries and revenue over 1 trillion rupees. Founded 1975. B2B tier-one supplier with low consumer awareness.

Deutsche Lufthansa AG is Europe's largest airline group by revenue, with Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian, Brussels Airlines, Eurowings and ITA Airways, plus Lufthansa Technik and LSG catering. It flies about 120 million passengers a year, with revenue around 37 billion euros. Headquartered in Cologne, with hubs in Frankfurt and Munich (Crunchbase lists Frankfurt). Listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (LHA). Very strong global consumer brand, with a track record of sports partnerships.

wiki.title: Lufthansa
wiki.text: Deutsche Lufthansa AG, trading as Lufthansa Group, is a German aviation holding company. Its principal airline, Lufthansa German Airlines is the flag carrier of Germany. Lufthansa Group is the second-largest airline group in Europe by passengers carried, as well as largest in Europe and fourth largest in the world by revenue. Lufthansa Airlines is also one of the five founding members of Star Alliance, the world's largest airline alliance, established in 1997.

about: Embraer is a Brazilian aerospace manufacturer making E-Jets and E2 regional airliners, Phenom and Praetor business jets, the C-390 Millennium military transport and defence and security systems, plus services and eVTOL development through Eve. Headquartered in Sao Jose dos Campos, Brazil (the Saudi Arabia country tag looks wrong). Customers are airlines, governments and private jet owners, with revenue around $6 billion or more. Listed on B3 (EMBR3) and NYSE (ERJ). Well-known in aviation, with limited consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Embraer
wiki.text: Embraer S.A. is a Brazilian multinational aerospace corporation. It develops and manufactures aircraft and aviation systems, and provides leasing, equipment, and technical support services. Embraer is the third largest producer of civil aircraft after Boeing and Airbus. The company also has a significant presence in military aviation, ranking among the top 100 defense contractors. It is headquartered in São José dos Campos, São Paulo, with offices and operations in China, the Netherlands, Portugal, Singapore, and the United States.

about: Coherent Corp., formerly II-VI Incorporated, makes engineered materials, lasers and optical networking components, including silicon carbide wafers and devices, datacom transceivers for AI data centres, and industrial and medical lasers. Customers are telecom and data centre operators, industrial and semiconductor manufacturers, with revenue of about $5 billion. Headquartered in Saxonburg, Pennsylvania. Listed on NYSE (COHR). B2B photonics supplier with little consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Coherent Corp.
wiki.text: Coherent Corp. is an American manufacturer of optical materials and semiconductors. As of 2023, the company had 26,622 employees. Its stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol COHR. In 2022, II-VI acquired laser manufacturer Coherent, Inc., and adopted its name.

about: Polaris Inc. is a US manufacturer of powersports vehicles: off-road vehicles (RZR, Ranger, General), snowmobiles, Indian Motorcycle, Slingshot three-wheelers, Polaris boats and defence vehicles through Polaris Government and Defense. Sales are about 7 billion dollars annually and customers are consumers, dealers and military buyers, sold in North America and overseas. Founded in 1954 in Roseau, Minnesota, headquartered in Medina, Minnesota (Crunchbase shows Ohio) and listed on the NYSE (PII). Strong consumer brand in motorsports and outdoor recreation, with a long history of racing sponsorships.

wiki.title: Polaris
wiki.what: Northern pole-star; brightest star in Ursa Minor
wiki.text: Polaris is a yellow supergiant star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Ursa Minor. It is designated α Ursae Minoris and is commonly called the North Star. With an apparent magnitude that fluctuates around 1.98, it is the brightest star in the constellation and is readily visible to the naked eye at night. The position of the star lies less than 1° away from the north celestial pole, making it the current northern pole star. The stable position of the star in the Northern Sky makes it useful for navigation.

wiki.title: Polaris Inc.
wiki.text: Polaris Inc. is an American automotive manufacturer headquartered in Medina, Minnesota, United States. Polaris was founded in Roseau, Minnesota, where it still has engineering and manufacturing facilities. The company manufactured motorcycles through its Victory Motorcycles subsidiary until January 2017, then produced motorcycles through the Indian Motorcycle subsidiary, which it purchased in April 2011 and announced its divestiture in October 2025. Polaris produced personal watercraft from 1994 to 2004. The company was originally named Polaris Industries Inc. and was renamed in 2019 to Polaris Inc.

about: Air Canada is Canada's largest airline and flag carrier, based in Montreal, with a global network of 200 destinations, operating mainline and regional services plus the Aeroplan loyalty programme and Air Canada Rouge. It is a Star Alliance member, listed on the TSX (AC), with about 40,000 employees and revenue over 20 billion Canadian dollars. Customers are leisure and business travellers worldwide. Very high consumer visibility in Canada, and a long-standing sponsor of sports and events including the Olympics.

wiki.title: Air Canada
wiki.text: Air Canada is the flag carrier and the largest airline of Canada by fleet size and passengers carried. Headquartered in the borough of Saint-Laurent in Montreal, the airline was founded in 1937 and operates a fleet of 335 aircraft serving 208 destinations worldwide through its major hubs at Montréal–Trudeau, Toronto–Pearson and Vancouver. It is a founding member of Star Alliance. In 2025, the airline transported 45.3 million passengers.

about: GE Aerospace is the independent jet and turboprop engine maker that emerged in April 2024 when General Electric completed the spin-off of GE Vernova, after earlier splitting off GE HealthCare. Based in Evendale near Cincinnati, Ohio, it makes engines through GE and its CFM joint venture with Safran for aircraft like the Boeing 737 and Airbus A320, plus defence engines and services. Listed on the NYSE (GE), with revenue of about 40 billion dollars. B2B brand with strong aviation visibility.

wiki.title: GE Aerospace
wiki.text: General Electric Company is an American aircraft engine supplier that is headquartered in Evendale, Ohio, outside Cincinnati. It is the legal successor to the original General Electric Company founded in 1892, which split into three separate companies between November 2021 and April 2024, adopting the trade name GE Aerospace after divesting its healthcare and energy divisions.

about: Dassault Systemes is a French software company based in Velizy-Villacoublay, listed on Euronext Paris (DSY), which sells 3D design, simulation and product lifecycle management software, including CATIA, SOLIDWORKS, SIMULIA and the 3DEXPERIENCE platform. Customers are industrial manufacturers in aerospace, automotive, life sciences and consumer goods, with revenue of about 6 billion euros. It is a long-standing technology partner in motorsport engineering. B2B, with high awareness among engineers but little among the general public.

wiki.title: Dassault Systèmes
wiki.text: Dassault Systèmes SE is a French multinational software corporation which develops software for 3D product design, simulation, manufacturing and other 3D related products.

about: Airbus is the European aerospace and defence manufacturer, legally based in Leiden, Netherlands with main operations in Toulouse, Hamburg and Seville. It builds the A320, A350 and A380 airliners, H-series helicopters, military aircraft and satellites, with revenue of about 69 billion euros and 150,000 employees. Customers are airlines, lessors and governments. Listed on Euronext Paris (AIR). Recognised worldwide and a prolific sponsor, including of sport and events.

wiki.title: Airbus
wiki.text: Airbus SE is a European aerospace corporation. While the company's primary business is the design and manufacture of commercial aircraft, it also operates separate divisions for Defence and Space and Helicopters. Airbus has long been the world's leading helicopter manufacturer and, in 2019, emerged as the world's largest manufacturer of airliners.

about: Larsen & Toubro (L&T) is a Mumbai-based Indian engineering and construction conglomerate, listed on the NSE and BSE, that builds infrastructure, power plants, buildings, hydrocarbon projects, defence equipment and IT services (LTIMindtree). Revenue is above 2 trillion rupees, with about 400,000 employees. A major national industrial brand, well known in India, and it sponsors some sporting events.

wiki.title: Larsen & Toubro
wiki.text: Larsen & Toubro Limited (L&T) is an Indian multinational conglomerate headquartered in Mumbai. It operates in sectors including industrial technology, heavy industry, engineering, construction, manufacturing, power, information technology, defence, and financial services.

about: Aena is the Spanish state-controlled airport operator, headquartered in Madrid, managing 46 airports in Spain and stakes in airports abroad such as London Luton and Brazil, and handling over 300 million passengers a year. Revenue comes from airport charges and retail. Majority owned by ENAIRE (the state), listed on Spain's stock exchange (AENA). Well-known infrastructure brand in Spain, with large passenger reach.

wiki.title: ENAIRE
wiki.text: Enaire or AENA is the air navigation manager in Spain, certified for the provision of enroute, approach and aerodrome control services. As a public corporate entity attached to the Spanish Ministry of Public Works, it is responsible for air traffic control, aeronautical information and the communication, navigation and surveillance networks so air companies and their aircraft can fly safely and in an organised format within Spanish airspace.

about: Air India is India's flag carrier, based in Gurugram, Haryana, operating domestic and international flights; it was founded by JRD Tata in 1932, nationalised, and returned to the Tata Group in 2022, then merged with Vistara in 2024 and with AirAsia India, and it has placed one of the largest aircraft orders in history. Strong consumer brand across India and the diaspora, with sports sponsorship history.

wiki.title: Air India
wiki.text: Air India is the flag carrier of India, headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana. The airline is owned by Air India Limited, which is owned by the Tata Group (74.9%) and Singapore Airlines (25.1%). The airline is a member of Star Alliance since 11 July 2014. As of November 2025, the airline serves 87 domestic and international destinations, from its primary hub at Indira Gandhi International Airport, and secondary hubs at Kempegowda International Airport and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport. The airline operates a fleet of Airbus and Boeing aircraft, and is the second-largest airline in India by passenger volume, after IndiGo.

about: Divergent Technologies is a Torrance, California advanced manufacturing company that uses AI-driven design and metal 3D printing in its Divergent Adaptive Production System to build lightweight structures for cars, aerospace and defense. Customers include Aston Martin, McLaren, Bugatti and defense contractors. It makes the Czinger hypercar through sister company Czinger. Crunchbase shows about $1.1 billion in funding. Strong motorsport and high-performance automotive connections.

Textron is a Providence, Rhode Island industrial conglomerate whose brands include Cessna and Beechcraft aircraft, Bell helicopters and tiltrotors, Textron Systems, E-Z-GO golf cars and Arctic Cat snowmobiles, with revenue of about $14 billion. Customers include business jet operators, militaries and golf courses. Listed on the NYSE (TXT). Founded in 1923. Well-known aerospace and vehicle brands, with golf and recreation sponsorships.

wiki.title: Textron
wiki.text: Textron Inc. is an American industrial conglomerate based in Providence, Rhode Island. Textron's subsidiaries include Bell Textron, Kautex, Textron Aviation, and Lycoming Engines. It was founded by Royal Little in 1923 as the Special Yarns Company.

about: Lufthansa Group is Europe's largest airline group, operating Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines, Eurowings and Discover, plus Lufthansa Technik and catering businesses. It flies over 100 million passengers a year to hundreds of destinations, with revenue of roughly 35 billion euros. It is headquartered in Cologne, and Frankfurt is its main hub. It is listed in Frankfurt (LHA). Lufthansa is a major consumer brand and an established sports and event sponsor in Germany and Europe.

wiki.title: Lufthansa
wiki.text: Deutsche Lufthansa AG, trading as Lufthansa Group, is a German aviation holding company. Its principal airline, Lufthansa German Airlines is the flag carrier of Germany. Lufthansa Group is the second-largest airline group in Europe by passengers carried, as well as largest in Europe and fourth largest in the world by revenue. Lufthansa Airlines is also one of the five founding members of Star Alliance, the world's largest airline alliance, established in 1997.
